📖 Reading & Listening

Reading The Warm Bread

0 / 0

It was a difficult week for Sama. Her grades were slipping, and she felt overwhelmed by all her schoolwork. On Thursday afternoon, she sat by her window, staring at the grey sky that seemed to mirror her mood. She hadn't spoken to many people lately and felt isolated from her friends. Then, there was a knock at the door. It was Mrs. Aya, the friendly neighbor who lived upstairs. She held a small basket covered with a clean white cloth still warm from the oven. "I baked some fresh bread this morning," Mrs. Aya said warmly. "I thought you might like some."

The smell was irresistible, wrapping around Sama like a gentle hug. Sama smiled for the first time in days and invited her in for tea. They sat together, chatting about small things – school, plants, and Mrs. Aya's garden, while the soft sound of rain tapped on the window. Slowly, Sama felt her worries began to fade. Before leaving, Mrs. Aya said, "Sometimes, the smallest kindness can make a big difference." Sama kept thinking about those words. She decided to help her younger cousin with homework that evening. Seeing her cousin's face light up filled her with optimism. She realized that kindness doesn't just make others feel better; it can change your own heart, too.

Listening Planting Trees, Growing Myself

0 / 0

My name is Ahmed, and I'm 17 years old. Last year, I joined a community tree-planting project in my village. At first, I only wanted to get volunteering hours for school. But what happened during the project truly transformed me. We worked in teams to dig holes, plant saplings, and water them. It was hard work under the hot sun, but we laughed a lot and supported each other.

I learned the meaning of real teamwork – not just working together, but caring if someone was tired or needed water.

One day, an old farmer came to watch. He said, "I haven't seen green like this in 20 years." His words stayed in my mind. I realized we weren't just planting trees – we were making a difference to the environment and to people's lives.

After three months, I felt different. I had more confidence to speak up, and I cared more about my community. Volunteering taught me responsibility – those trees depend on us. I even started a recycling corner at school.

Now, I believe volunteering isn't only about helping others. It's also about personal growth. You give time, but you get so much more – skills, friends, and pride. I will continue volunteering because it has become a lifelong habit. And yes, it's meaningful. When you serve others, your heart grows bigger.

📘 Language — Part 1 · القواعد

Giving Advice إسداء النصح: should & shouldn't

Useالاستخدام
نستخدم should / shouldn't للنصيحة: لنقول إن شيئًا ما جيد (ينبغى فعله) أو غير جيد (لا ينبغى فعله).
بعد should / shouldn't يأتى الفعل فى المصدر (بدون أى إضافات وبدون to)، وتأتى مع جميع الضمائر والأسماء مفردًا كان أو جمعًا.
  • You should always wash your hands after you've touched the cat.
  • Tourists should wear sun cream when it's very hot.
  • You shouldn't walk too much in the sun.
  • You shouldn't touch that. It's dirty!
  • In summer, tourists should wear a hat and ought not to sit in the sun.
Questionالسؤال
Should + فاعل + مصدر + تكملة الجملة …… ؟  (ويكون معناه «هل يجب …؟»)
أداة استفهام + should / shouldn't + subject + verb …… ؟
  • Should you go to school every day? – Yes, I should. / No, I shouldn't.
  • What should I try doing? – You should definitely try some windsurfing.
Passiveالمبنى للمجهول
مفعول + should / shouldn't + be + P.P.
  • You should eat a lot of vegetables and fruits as they are healthy. (active)
  • A lot of vegetables and fruits should be eaten as they are healthy. (passive)

بدائل should & shouldn't مصطلحات النصيحة

Should ينبغىShouldn't لا ينبغى
You ought to + inf.You ought not to + inf.
If I were you, I would + inf.If I were you, I wouldn't + inf.
I advise you to + inf.I advise you not to + inf.
My advice to you is to + inf.My advice to you is not to + inf.
You had better + inf.You'd better not + inf.
It is better to + inf.It is better not to + inf.
It is advisable for …… to + inf.It is inadvisable for …… to + inf.
It is desirable for …… to + inf.It is undesirable for …… to + inf.
It is important for … to + inf.It is important for … not to + inf.
It will be a good idea to + inf.It will be a good idea not to + inf.

Modal verbs of regret (blame) اللوم والندم

should (ought to) have + P.P.  /  shouldn't (ought not to) have + P.P.
للتعبير عن اللوم أو الندم على فعل أو عدم فعل شيء فى الماضى.
  • You shouldn't have arrived late for your exam.
  • I'm sorry! I ought to have come on time.

Obligation & Necessity الإلزام والضرورة: must / mustn't

Useالاستخدام
نستخدم must / mustn't للتعبير عن الإلزام أو الضرورة أو التحريم، ويأتى بعدها الفعل فى المصدر بدون to، وتأتى مع جميع الضمائر والأسماء.
  • You must follow the traffic rules. (القواعد والقوانين)
  • I must work hard for the exams next week. (إلزام شخصى)
  • I must buy a present for my mother. (مشاعر قوية)
  • You must come to my party tonight. (دعوة قوية)
  • They mustn't eat that cheese. It's green! – You must stop smoking. (نصيحة قوية)
  • We must buy souvenirs for our friends here. (تذكرة بفعل شيء)
Questionالسؤال
Must + فاعل + مصدر + تكملة الجملة …… ؟  |  أداة استفهام + must / mustn't + subject + verb …… ؟
  • Must I turn right here? – Yes, you must.
  • What must I do to avoid traffic fines? – You must stick to the rules.
Passiveالمبنى للمجهول
مفعول + must / mustn't + be + P.P.
  • I must buy a present for my mother. (active)
  • A present must be bought for my mother. (passive)

بدائل must الضرورة والإلزام

must + مصدر = It's necessary / It's a necessity / It's a must / It's obligatory / It's lawful + for …. to + inf.
  • You must turn right. = It is necessary for you to turn right.
  • It is obligatory for you to turn right. – It is a necessity for you to turn right.
  • It is a must for you to turn right.
الكلمةالنوعملاحظة
mustفعل مساعد بمعنى «يجب»يأتى بعده المصدر مباشرة
a mustاسم بمعنى «ضرورة»يمكن أن يأتى بعدها to
necessaryصفة بمعنى «ضرورى»It is necessary for … to + inf.
a necessityاسم بمعنى «ضرورة»It is a necessity for … to + inf.

بدائل mustn't المنع والتحريم

البديلالمعنى
It's not allowed to + inf.ليس مسموحًا أن
It's not permitted to + inf.ليس مسموحًا أن
It's forbidden to + inf.مُحرَّم
It's prohibited to + inf.من الممنوع
It's banned to + inf.من الممنوع
It's against the law to + inf.ضد القانون أن
It's illegal to + inf.غير قانونى أن
  • You mustn't park your car here. = It is against the law to park your car here.
  • It is not allowed to park your car here. – It is not permitted to park your car here.
  • It is forbidden to park your car here. – It is banned to park your car here.
  • It is prohibited to park your car here. – It is illegal to park your car here.
ويمكن أيضًا استخدام mustn't للتعبير عن نصيحة قوية أو التزام شخصى، واستخدام can't للتعبير عن عدم السماح.
  • You mustn't waste your time. – I mustn't leave my bedroom untidy.
  • You can't smoke in hospitals.

have to / has to / need to إلزام مفروض علينا

Affirmationالإثبات
نستخدم have to / has to / need to للتعبير عن إلزام مفروض علينا، ويأتى بعدها الفعل فى المصدر.
has to / needs to مع المفرد he – she – it  |  have to / need to مع الجمع we – they – I – you.
  • We have to go to school on time. = We need to go to school on time.
  • She has to get a passport to travel to London.
Negationالنفى — انعدام الضرورة
don't have to / doesn't have to  |  don't need to / doesn't need to / needn't  + inf.
  • She doesn't have to hurry, she isn't late for school.
  • They don't have to buy bread; there is much in the fridge.

الخلاصة must · have to · need to

الفرق فى الاستخدام:
  • must + inf. — إلزام شخصى ومشاعر قوية وأمنيات ودعوات ونصيحة قوية وتذكير أنفسنا بشيء.
    I must work hard for the exams. – You must come to my party tonight.
  • have to / has to + inf. — مع القواعد أو عندما لا تمتلك اختيارًا لفعل شيء (مضطر إلى).
    We have to go to school every day. – We don't have to get up early. It's a holiday.
  • need to + inf. — الحاجة إلى شيء معين، ونفيها don't need to / needn't + inf.
    Hassan needs to go to the bank. – I needn't buy a new pen. I've already got one.
الصيغةما يأتى بعدها
must · mustn't · should · shouldn't · needn't+ مصدر بدون to
have · has · had · need(s)+ to + مصدر (to إجبارى)
don't have to = don't need to = needn't+ مصدر — عدم الضرورة
do/don't · does/doesn't · did/didn't · will/won't+ have to / need to
الماضىhad to + inf. · didn't have to + inf. · needn't have + P.P. · should have + P.P.
المجهولhave to / has to / had to / need to / should(n't) / must(n't) + be + P.P.

📖 Reading & Listening — Part 2

Reading Serving the Community in Times of Danger

0 / 0

My name is Radwan, and I work as a firefighter in Alexandria. Many people think our job is just putting out fires, but it's much more than that. We rescue people from car accidents, help during floods, and sometimes save animals trapped in dangerous places.

The truth is, our work can be risky. I have entered burning buildings where smoke made it hard to see and breathe. I've stood on shaking ladders in the middle of the night, with the heat almost burning my skin. Sadly, I have also seen lives lost before we could reach them. These moments stay with me forever.

Yet, we do it because we believe in obligation – the duty to help each other, no matter the cost. In every emergency, we must act quickly, stay calm, and trust our training. We don't think about fear in those moments; we think about the people waiting for us. I am proud to serve my community. I know that my work saves lives, and that is worth every risk. When you help others, you are not just doing a job – you are protecting hope itself.

Listening Voluntary Work

0 / 0

Voluntary work is an important part of building stronger communities and better societies. Unlike paid employment, voluntary work is done freely, without expecting financial rewards. People of all ages can participate, from young students to retired professionals, and their contributions make a visible difference in the lives of others.

One of the main values of voluntary work is that it teaches responsibility. When a person gives time to help others, they learn that their actions matter. For example, students who volunteer in hospitals or schools develop empathy and patience. They realize that even simple tasks, like reading stories to children or assisting elderly patients, bring joy and comfort. Everyone has to remember that helping others is essential. Voluntary work also strengthens social connections. People from different backgrounds meet.

They must cooperate and share experiences. This cooperation builds understanding and respect across cultures. Moreover, volunteering often gives individuals practical skills such as teamwork, problem-solving, and leadership which later help them in professional life.

Finally, voluntary work is a source of personal satisfaction so we all should participate in it. Knowing that one's efforts have supported others creates pride and motivation. It proves that true wealth is not only measured in money, but also in kindness and service.

🎯 Part 3 · Skills — المهارات

Writing A descriptive essay

Definitionالتعريف
  • A descriptive essay is writing that makes the reader imagine they are in the place or situation.
المقال الوصفى هو كتابة تجعل القارئ يتخيل أنه داخل المكان أو الموقف.
Structureالبناء
  • 1. Introduction – introduce the topic and why it matters. المقدمة: قدّم الموضوع ولماذا هو مهم
  • 2. Body Paragraphs – describe using senses (sight, hearing, smell, taste, touch). الفقرات: استخدم الحواس الخمس فى الوصف
  • 3. Conclusion – summarize and express your feeling. الخاتمة: لخّص وشارك شعورك
Sensesالحواس
  • Sight البصر — colors, shapes, size.
  • Hearing السمع — noises, whispers, music.
  • Smell الشم — flowers, salty air, food.
  • Taste التذوق — sweet, salty, spicy.
  • Touch اللمس — soft, rough, cold, warm.
Language Toolsأدوات اللغة
  • Use adjectives (describing words) → "tall trees, cold wind".
  • Use adverbs (describing actions) → she cried softly.
استخدم الصفات (للوصف) والظروف (لتوضيح الأفعال).
Feature السمةDescription الوصف
Focused Topic
موضوع مركَّز		▸ Talks about one main subject in detail.
يتحدث عن موضوع واحد رئيسى بتفصيل
Sensory Language
لغة الحواس		▸ Uses words that make you see, hear, smell, taste, or feel something.
يستخدم كلمات تجعلك ترى أو تسمع أو تشم أو تتذوق أو تشعر بشىء
Imagery
الخيال التصويرى		▸ Helps the reader picture things clearly in their mind.
يساعد القارئ على تخيّل الأشياء بوضوح فى ذهنه
Organized Structure
بنية منظمة		▸ Ideas are in order (by place, time, or theme).
الأفكار مرتبة حسب المكان أو الزمن أو الموضوع
Figurative Language
اللغة المجازية		▸ Uses creative comparisons like similes and metaphors.
يستخدم مقارنات إبداعية مثل التشبيهات والاستعارات
Emotional Impact
الأثر العاطفى		▸ Shares a feeling or mood, like happiness, peace, or sadness.
ينقل شعورًا أو مزاجًا مثل السعادة أو السلام أو الحزن

اكتب فقرة من (٨٠) كلمة عن الموضوع الآتى:
  • "Helping your friends at school"
  • يمكنك الاستعانة بالأفكار الآتية: Explaining difficult lessons – exchanging tools – giving advice
✍️ Model answer نموذج إجابة
Helping your friends at school
Helping your friends at school is a great value that makes our school life happier. When a friend cannot understand a difficult lesson, I try to explain it to him simply and patiently. We must also exchange tools such as pens, rulers and books, because a small act of kindness costs nothing but means a lot. Moreover, giving good advice to a friend who has a problem shows real empathy. Helping others builds trust, strengthens friendship and creates a strong, cooperative community. In short, hands that help make hearts that care.

In recent years, many schools have adopted digital learning tools to enhance students' education. One school, Bright Future Academy, has gained recognition for its innovative approach. Instead of relying solely on traditional textbooks, the school includes interactive apps, online quizzes, and virtual simulations.

Bright Future Academy believes that learning should be engaging and personalized. Students are encouraged to explore topics independently while teachers provide guidance and regular feedback. This approach helps students stay motivated and prevents boredom during lessons. The school also emphasizes collaboration, allowing students to work in teams and learn from each other's points of view.

To monitor progress, the school regularly collects data through assessments and surveys. Students report that the learning environment is both exciting and supportive, as it allows them to take ownership of their education. The results have been positive: student participation has increased, test scores have improved, and teachers have noticed greater enthusiasm in the classroom.

Bright Future Academy demonstrates that technology can enhance learning when combined with thoughtful strategies. By integrating modern tools with student-centered approaches, the school proves that educational success does not depend solely on traditional methods.

1Why has Bright Future Academy gained recognition?
2The word "personalized" in the passage most nearly means: ……… .

4Teachers at Bright Future Academy mainly act as: ……… .

Write a descriptive essay of (150) words about the following
"My Grandpa's House"
✍️Model answer نموذج إجابة
My Grandpa's House
My grandpa's house is my favourite place in the whole world. It stands at the end of a narrow street, with old white walls and a wooden door that makes a soft sound whenever it opens. In front of it, a tall lemon tree fills the air with a fresh, sweet smell every morning.
Inside, the rooms are simple but warm. The floor is made of smooth stone that feels cool under my feet in summer. In the living room, there is an old sofa, a small radio and a big clock that ticks quietly all day. I can still hear my grandma calling us for lunch and smell the fresh bread coming from the oven.
In the evening, we all sit in the small garden, drinking tea and listening to my grandpa's stories about the past. His voice is calm and full of wisdom.
Whenever I visit that house, I feel safe, loved and peaceful. It is not just a building of stone; it is a home full of memories that will stay in my heart forever.
